_comment: TOOL ALLOWLISTS ARE SECURITY CONTROLS, not conveniences. Both MCP servers are wrapped by mcp-guard/mcp-guard.js, which hides
and rejects every tool not in the server's policy (mcp-guard/policies/*.js) and checks arguments. toolFilter is a second layer
applied by ollama-mcp-bridge. Do not widen either list without a security review.
GitHub = HUMAN-IN-THE-LOOP ENFORCEMENT: the agent may only read files, create a security/fix-* branch, commit to it, and open a
pull request; a human must review and merge. agent_prompt.md's instruction to 'open a PR' is NOT a control: an LLM can ignore it.
@modelcontextprotocol/server-github has no allowlist of its own; the guard blocks merge_pull_request, push_files [force-pushes],
fork/create repository, etc., any write to a branch outside security/fix-*, and any call for a repository other than TARGET_REPO.
Trivy = LEAST PRIVILEGE: only vulnerability scans of MCP_GUARD_SCAN_ROOT. scan_repository and scan_image (arbitrary remote fetches)
are blocked, as are scans of other paths and the secret/misconfig/license scanners.

trivy._comment: Official Trivy MCP plugin (aquasecurity/trivy-mcp); version pinned and checksum-verified in the Dockerfile. The npm package previously referenced here (@aquasecurity/mcp-server-trivy) does not exist.

github._comment_env: The bridge passes MCP servers only HOME/PATH/etc., so the token must be forwarded explicitly, to this server only (Trivy never sees it).
